articles.title: Ethnic cleansing, siege and collective punishment: The records of Israel’s incoming MPs
articles.summary:
Ethnic cleansing, siege and collective punishment: The records of Israel’s incoming MPs

Israel’s projected next parliament includes politicians who have advocated collective punishment of Palestinians, ethnic cleansing, genocide, pushed for the starvations of Palestinians in Gaza and opposed Palestinian statehood.

The following candidates are on course to enter or return to the Knesset, according to provisional results.

Hanamel Dorfman - Jewish Power

Ben Gvir’s former chief of staff comes from the extremist Jewish settler movement. Haaretz quoted a 17-year-old Dorfman at a protest against African asylum seekers in Tel Aviv as saying: “The only problem with the Nazis is that I was on the losing side". Footage from his 2013 wedding showed him brandishing knives while dancing to songs calling for attacks on Palestinians.

Yitzhak Wasserlauf - Jewish Power

Wasserlauf invoked a biblical passage celebrating the killing of infants to motivate soldiers heading into Gaza. Jewish News reported that the recorded call documented him quoting Psalm 137, including its reference to seizing babies and smashing them against rocks.

Tzvika Mor - Religious Zionism–Zehut

The Kiryat Arba settler has openly promoted collective punishment. In an October radio interview, he demanded electricity and water cut-offs for Palestinian villages who resisted Jewish occupation, alongside the expulsion of their families and confiscation of their property.

Itamar Eitam - Religious Zionism–Zehut

The reserve lieutenant colonel has rejected the distinction between fighters and Palestinian civilians in Gaza, a common view in Israeli society. In a separate July 2024 interview, he portrayed Palestinians as evil and dismissed the idea that they simply wanted peaceful lives and an education for their children, like any other people.

Yonatan Shalev - Together

A combat reservist who served in Gaza during the genocide, Shalev has defended denying Palestinians a state. He told The Jerusalem Post that Bennett would not allow Palestinian statehood: “We’re not going to pass Israeli territory to anyone,” he said said of Palestinian land.

Yulia Malinovsky - Yisrael Beiteinu

Malinovsky joined activists blocking Gaza-bound aid trucks on 22 October, turning the obstruction of supplies into election campaigning. She publicised the blockade while accusing Netanyahu’s government of delivering food to Palestinians men, women and children instead of starving them.

Matan Kahana - Yashar

Kahana said in June 2022 that he would press a hypothetical button to remove Arabs and send them to Switzerland. The remark expressed a desire for mass ethnic cleansing and referred to Arabs generally, rather than specifically to Palestinians in Gaza.

Merav Ben-Ari - Together

During an October 2023 parliamentary debate, Ben-Ari blamed Palestinian children for their own suffering and rejected comparisons with Israeli children killed. A subsequent UN inquiry cited her remarks in its examination of rhetoric targeting Gaza’s children.

articles.title: ‘Every baby in Gaza is an enemy’: Who are Israel’s incoming MPs and what do they believe?
articles.summary:
‘Every baby in Gaza is an enemy’: Who are Israel’s incoming MPs and what do they believe?

Moshe Feiglin, who has called for the ethnic cleansing of Gaza’s entire Palestinian population and branded Palestinian babies enemies, is projected to return to Israel’s parliament.

The Zehut leader ran second on a joint list with the far-right Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism party, which is on course to secure six seats. The count remains provisional.

Feiglin has repeatedly targeted Palestinian children in his statements about Gaza.

“Every child, every baby in Gaza is an enemy,” he said on Channel 14 in May 2025, during remarks opposing humanitarian aid entering the territory.

In June 2024, he invoked Adolf Hitler during a Channel 12 discussion, drawing a parallel between Hitler’s determination to eliminate Jews and his own demand that no Palestinian should remain in Gaza.

He renewed his calls for ethnic cleansing in an interview with The Jerusalem Post this month.

“Occupation, transfer all, all the Arabs. I don’t care,” he said.

In a separate i24NEWS interview this month, Feiglin endorsed expelling everyone, including premature newborns, from Gaza.

articles.title: Arab Israelis wake to new political dawn after record election success
‘Jewish supremacy is the law of the land’
articles.summary:
‘Jewish supremacy is the law of the land’

Middle East Eye spoke to Antony Loewenstein, an independent journalist, film-maker and author of The Palestine Laboratory, about the Israeli election results.

“There's not really any major or even significant difference between Netanyahu and the so-called opposition on any of the key issues - Iran, Lebanon, Gaza, the West Bank - and in some ways, although at this point it's obviously unclear who won and Netanyahu seems to be slightly ahead with his bloc, but obviously that could change in the coming days or weeks,” Loewenstein told MEE.

“But really what that says, I think, is something much bigger. Which is that a sizeable proportion, if not the majority, of Israeli Jewish voters do not want to engage with Arabs, do not want Arabs in government, do not believe in any self-determination for Arabs, and do not want any real change between the West Bank and Gaza. And in fact a sizeable proportion, if not a majority, want to get rid of all Arabs from Palestine and as many Arabs from Israel itself, which really I think speaks to the fact that the issue in Israel, as many people like me have been saying for years, is not just about Netanyahu.”

“Obviously, it's very significant that the Arab parties have won hugely, and that's probably because many Palestinians voted in Israel, and also probably more left-wing Israelis, including some Israeli Jewish friends of mine who wanted to support the Arab Parties,” he added. 

“And in a sane country, those voters and those parties would have representation in a government, or at least in a sizable opposition. But at this current point it's very hard to see if that will happen because both major parties, the opposition and Netanyahu, have refused doing so. So really it just shows that Jewish supremacy is the law of the land,” Loewenstein concluded.

Jordánsko mezitím provedlo ozbrojený úder v Sýrii v reakci na předchozí incident, zatímco v Kuvajtu proběhly přísné rozsudky kvůli napojení na Írán a Hezbollah.
archive.security_status_en: Israel is holding pivotal parliamentary elections accompanied by high voter turnout and friction in the West Bank and around polling stations. Meanwhile, Jordan carried out a deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for a prior incident, and Kuwait handed down severe sentences over Iran-Hezbollah links.
archive.forecast_cs: V následujících dnech se očekává postupné sčítání hlasů a vyhodnocení výsledků izraelských voleb, které mohou výrazně ovlivnit směřování země. Lze také sledovat diplomatické dozvuky a reakce na přeshraniční aktivity v Sýrii a Kuvajtu.
archive.forecast_en: The coming days will see the gradual vote counting and evaluation of the Israeli election results, which could significantly steer the country's trajectory. Diplomatic reverberations and reactions to cross-border activities in Syria and Kuwait are also expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Izrael čelí hluboké politické nestabilitě po předčasných volbách do Knesetu, kde se dosavadní blok premiéra Netanjahua propadl na 57 křesel a výsledek zůstává otevřený. Mezitím pokračují regionální třenice, včetně jordánských úderů v Sýrii a vzniku nového společného bezpečnostního výboru mezi oběma státy. Írán nadále zůstává centrem diplomatického i geopolitického tlaku, zatímco humanitární a bezpečnostní situace v Gaze a Západním břehu Jordánu vyvolává ostré mezinárodní odsouzení.
archive.security_status_en: Israel is facing deep political instability following the Knesset elections, where Prime Minister Netanyahu's bloc has dropped to 57 seats and the final outcome remains deadlocked. Meanwhile, regional frictions persist, including Jordanian strikes in Syria and the establishment of a new joint security committee between the two nations. Iran remains the focal point of intense diplomatic and geopolitical maneuvering, while the humanitarian and security situation in Gaza and the West Bank draws sharp international criticism.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech se očekává postupné dokončení sčítání hlasů v Izraeli a intenzivní vyjednávání o formování koaliční vlády. Zároveň budou pokračovat diplomatické snahy ohledně bezpečnostní situace na syrsko-jordánské hranici.
archive.forecast_en: The coming days are expected to see the finalization of vote counting in Israel and intensive negotiations regarding the formation of a coalition government. Simultaneously, diplomatic efforts concerning security on the Syrian-Jordanian border will continue.

archive.security_status_cs: Izraelské parlamentní volby skončily patem, přičemž arabské strany se rýsují jako klíčoví hráči při sestavování vlády uprostřed pokračujících bojů v Gaze a na Západním břehu. USA přesouvají systém Patriot do regionu v očekávání možných úderů souvisejících s Íránem, zatímco v Sýrii probíhají historická jednání o obchodu a bezpečnosti s Irákem.
archive.security_status_en: Israeli parliamentary elections have resulted in a deadlock, with Arab parties emerging as potential kingmakers amid ongoing hostilities in Gaza and the West Bank. The US is relocating a Patriot missile system to the region in anticipation of potential Iran-related strikes, while landmark trade and security talks are underway between Iraq and post-Assad Syria.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech budou pokračovat intenzivní politická jednání o sestavení izraelské vlády a sledování bezpečnostní situace v okolí íránské hranice. Očekává se také vyjasnění dopadů ropného incidentu v Hormuzském průlivu.
archive.forecast_en: The coming days will see intense political negotiations over forming an Israeli government and close monitoring of security developments regarding Iran. Clarification on the impacts of the Strait of Hormuz oil spill is also expected.
